Keep the rest of mod.rs as it is (line timing, affine reference points, accessors, render_line's layer collection). Other workers own obj.rs, bg_affine.rs and bitmap.rs.

Contract (on main, commit "refactor(ppu): layer line contract"):
- `compose_line(&mut self, line, layers: &LineLayers)`. `LineLayers` holds `backgrounds[4]` and `background_enabled[4]`, `sprites` (front-most sprite pixel per x, with OBJ `priority` and `is_semi_transparent_sprite`), `sprites_enabled` (DISPCNT OBJ on) and `obj_window[240]` (pixels inside the OBJ window).
- Each layer's `color` is BGR555 and `priority` 0-3; transparent pixels have `is_transparent`.
- Helpers: `ppu.register(offset)` gives raw WIN0H/WIN1H/WIN0V/WIN1V/WININ/WINOUT/MOSAIC/BLDCNT/BLDALPHA/BLDY; `dispcnt()`; `palette_color(0)` is the backdrop.

Scope:
- Windows 0/1, the OBJ window and the outside area. Each controls layer enables and the colour special effect enable. Handle window coordinate edge cases: x2 > 240 or x1 > x2, the same for y (gbatek: LCD I/O Window Feature).
- Colour special effects: alpha blending with EVA/EVB, brightness increase and decrease with EVY. First and second targets include the backdrop. A semi-transparent sprite always alpha-blends when the pixel below it is a second target, regardless of BLDCNT mode (gbatek: LCD I/O Color Special Effects).
- BG mosaic (gbatek: LCD I/O Mosaic Function). Implement it as a post-pass on each BG's `[LayerPixel; 240]` inside compose or a helper, horizontal and vertical, using BGxCNT bit 6. If vertical mosaic needs the renderers to sample a different line, describe that as a contract change for the integrator instead of editing mod.rs's render_line. OBJ mosaic belongs to the sprites worker.
- Priority: lower value wins; a sprite beats a BG of the same priority; BG0 beats BG3 on ties.
Keep it fast: no per-line allocation, per pixel only simple integer math.

- Unit tests.
- Dev ROMs via run_rom: $GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/test/tonc/win-demo.gba, tonc/bld-demo.gba, tonc/mos-demo.gba, tonc/prio-demo.gba, destoer/window-midframe.gba ($GBA_EVAL=/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval). Sprites are a stub on your branch, so judge BG-only parts.

# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fast feedback: grade a wasm against only the testcases you name.
#
#   scripts/grade-subset.sh <wasm> <run-name> <testcase-id>...
#   scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm cpu aw-arm-alu mgba-carry
#
# Builds a throwaway corpus (filtered testcases.json + the real ROMs,
# replays and reference cache mounted read-only) and runs the same
# gba-eval-grader docker image as the full grade. Results land in
# results/<run-name>/ in this repo. Section scores in summary.json are
# meaningless for a subset (missing subsystems count as 0); read the
# per-testcase entries instead.
set -euo pipefail

GBA_EVAL="${GBA_EVAL:-/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval}"
[ $# -ge 3 ] || { sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 2; }
WASM="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd)/$(basename "$1")"; NAME="$2"; shift 2
[ -f "$WASM" ] || { echo "error: $WASM not found" >&2; exit 1; }

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
OUT="$ROOT/results/$NAME"; SUBSET="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$SUBSET"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$OUT"

python3 -I - "$GBA_EVAL/corpus/testcases.json" "$SUBSET/testcases.json" "$@" <<'PY'
import json, sys
src, dst, *ids = sys.argv[1:]
data = json.load(open(src))
cases = data if isinstance(data, list) else data["testcases"]
picked = [c for c in cases if c["id"] in ids]
missing = set(ids) - {c["id"] for c in picked}
if missing:
    sys.exit(f"unknown testcase id(s): {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
json.dump(picked if isinstance(data, list) else {**data, "testcases": picked}, open(dst, "w"), indent=1)
PY
cp "$GBA_EVAL/corpus/grader.yaml" "$SUBSET/"

docker run --rm \
    -v "$GBA_EVAL":/repo:ro \
    -v "$SUBSET":/subset \

  LCD I/O Window Feature

The Window Feature may be used to split the screen into four regions. The
BG0-3,OBJ layers and Color Special Effects can be separately enabled or
disabled in each of these regions.

The DISPCNT Register
DISPCNT Bits 13-15 are used to enable Window 0, Window 1, and/or OBJ Window
regions, if any of these regions is enabled then the "Outside of Windows"
region is automatically enabled, too.
DISPCNT Bits 8-12 are kept used as master enable bits for the BG0-3,OBJ layers,
a layer is displayed only if both DISPCNT and WININ/OUT enable bits are set.

4000040h - WIN0H - Window 0 Horizontal Dimensions (W)
4000042h - WIN1H - Window 1 Horizontal Dimensions (W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0-7   X2, Rightmost coordinate of window, plus 1
  8-15  X1, Leftmost coordinate of window

Garbage values of X2>240 or X1>X2 are interpreted as X2=240.

4000044h - WIN0V - Window 0 Vertical Dimensions (W)
4000046h - WIN1V - Window 1 Vertical Dimensions (W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0-7   Y2, Bottom-most coordinate of window, plus 1
  8-15  Y1, Top-most coordinate of window

Garbage values of Y2>160 or Y1>Y2 are interpreted as Y2=160.

4000048h - WININ - Control of Inside of Window(s) (R/W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0-3   Window 0 BG0-BG3 Enable Bits     (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  4     Window 0 OBJ Enable Bit          (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  5     Window 0 Color Special Effect    (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  6-7   Not used
  8-11  Window 1 BG0-BG3 Enable Bits     (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  12    Window 1 OBJ Enable Bit          (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  13    Window 1 Color Special Effect    (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  14-15 Not used


400004Ah - WINOUT - Control of Outside of Windows & Inside of OBJ Window (R/W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0-3   Outside BG0-BG3 Enable Bits      (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  4     Outside OBJ Enable Bit           (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  5     Outside Color Special Effect     (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  6-7   Not used
  8-11  OBJ Window BG0-BG3 Enable Bits   (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  12    OBJ Window OBJ Enable Bit        (0=No Display, 1=Display)
  13    OBJ Window Color Special Effect  (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  14-15 Not used


The OBJ Window
The dimension of the OBJ Window is specified by OBJs which are having the "OBJ
Mode" attribute being set to "OBJ Window". Any non-transparent dots of any such
OBJs are marked as OBJ Window area. The OBJ itself is not displayed.
The color, palette, and display priority of these OBJs are ignored. Both
DISPCNT Bits 12 and 15 must be set when defining OBJ Window region(s).

Window Priority
In case that more than one window is enabled, and that these windows do
overlap, Window 0 is having highest priority, Window 1 medium, and Obj Window
lowest priority. Outside of Window is having zero priority, it is used for all
dots which are not inside of any window region.





  
  LCD I/O Mosaic Function

400004Ch - MOSAIC - Mosaic Size (W)
The Mosaic function can be separately enabled/disabled for BG0-BG3 by
BG0CNT-BG3CNT Registers, as well as for each OBJ0-127 by OBJ attributes in OAM
memory. Also, setting all of the bits below to zero effectively disables the
mosaic function.

  Bit   Expl.
  0-3   BG Mosaic H-Size  (minus 1)
  4-7   BG Mosaic V-Size  (minus 1)
  8-11  OBJ Mosaic H-Size (minus 1)
  12-15 OBJ Mosaic V-Size (minus 1)
  16-31 Not used

Example: When setting H-Size to 5, then pixels 0-5 of each display row are
colorized as pixel 0, pixels 6-11 as pixel 6, pixels 12-17 as pixel 12, and so
on.

Normally, a 'mosaic-pixel' is colorized by the color of the upperleft covered
pixel. In many cases it might be more desireful to use the color of the pixel
in the center of the covered area - this effect may be gained by scrolling the
background (or by adjusting the OBJ position, as far as upper/left rows/columns
of OBJ are transparent).





  
  LCD I/O Color Special Effects

Two types of Special Effects are supported: Alpha Blending (Semi-Transparency)
allows to combine colors of two selected surfaces. Brightness Increase/Decrease
adjust the brightness of the selected surface.

4000050h - BLDCNT - Color Special Effects Selection (R/W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0     BG0 1st Target Pixel (Background 0)
  1     BG1 1st Target Pixel (Background 1)
  2     BG2 1st Target Pixel (Background 2)
  3     BG3 1st Target Pixel (Background 3)
  4     OBJ 1st Target Pixel (Top-most OBJ pixel)
  5     BD  1st Target Pixel (Backdrop)
  6-7   Color Special Effect (0-3, see below)
         0 = None                (Special effects disabled)
         1 = Alpha Blending      (1st+2nd Target mixed)
         2 = Brightness Increase (1st Target becomes whiter)
         3 = Brightness Decrease (1st Target becomes blacker)
  8     BG0 2nd Target Pixel (Background 0)
  9     BG1 2nd Target Pixel (Background 1)
  10    BG2 2nd Target Pixel (Background 2)
  11    BG3 2nd Target Pixel (Background 3)
  12    OBJ 2nd Target Pixel (Top-most OBJ pixel)
  13    BD  2nd Target Pixel (Backdrop)
  14-15 Not used

Selects the 1st Target layer(s) for special effects. For Alpha
Blending/Semi-Transparency, it does also select the 2nd Target layer(s), which
should have next lower display priority as the 1st Target.
However, any combinations are possible, including that all layers may be
selected as both 1st+2nd target, in that case the top-most pixel will be used
as 1st target, and the next lower pixel as 2nd target.

4000052h - BLDALPHA - Alpha Blending Coefficients (R/W) (not W)
Used for Color Special Effects Mode 1, and for Semi-Transparent OBJs.

  Bit   Expl.
  0-4   EVA Coefficient (1st Target) (0..16 = 0/16..16/16, 17..31=16/16)
  5-7   Not used
  8-12  EVB Coefficient (2nd Target) (0..16 = 0/16..16/16, 17..31=16/16)
  13-15 Not used

For this effect, the top-most non-transparent pixel must be selected as 1st
Target, and the next-lower non-transparent pixel must be selected as 2nd
Target, if so - and only if so, then color intensities of 1st and 2nd Target
are mixed together by using the parameters in BLDALPHA register, for each pixel
each R, G, B intensities are calculated separately:

  I = MIN ( 31, I1st*EVA + I2nd*EVB )

Otherwise - for example, if only one target exists, or if a non-transparent
non-2nd-target pixel is moved between the two targets, or if 2nd target has
higher display priority than 1st target - then only the top-most pixel is
displayed (at normal intensity, regardless of BLDALPHA).

4000054h - BLDY - Brightness (Fade-In/Out) Coefficient (W) (not R/W)
Used for Color Special Effects Modes 2 and 3.

  Bit   Expl.
  0-4   EVY Coefficient (Brightness) (0..16 = 0/16..16/16, 17..31=16/16)
  5-31  Not used

For each pixel each R, G, B intensities are calculated separately:

  I = I1st + (31-I1st)*EVY   ;For Brightness Increase
  I = I1st - (I1st)*EVY      ;For Brightness Decrease

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.

5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it

take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the

I built the line compositor, but grading is unfinished: both grading runs (main 4e3eddf and my branch) were stopped by the system for low memory while the session sat idle. I was told not to restart them, so I have no summary.json. The scores below are the per-frame match values (`replay_score_deduped`) from the per-test JSON files the runs wrote before they died. `cargo test` passes (102 tests, 4 of them new) and the wasm release build succeeds.

## 1. What I built and the commits
Branch `phase3/ppu-effects`, from 4e3eddf:
- `12147f0` feat(ppu): windows, colour effects, BG mosaic in line compositor
- `1a484a6` fix(ppu): OBJ window needs DISPCNT OBJ enable too

The compositor now lives in `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a74f182e8b7063d5e/src/ppu/effects.rs` as `impl Ppu { pub(super) fn compose_line }`. There are no per-line allocations, and each pixel only does integer compares and shifts.
- **Windows:** window 0, then window 1, then the OBJ window, then the outside area. A garbage end value (X2>240 or X1>X2, the same for Y with 160) is read as the screen edge. Each region's bits gate the BG and OBJ layers and the effects bit. When no window is on, everything is enabled.
- **Priority:** the compositor keeps the front two pixels, sorting on `priority*8 + order`, where OBJ is 0 and BG0-BG3 are 1-4. So lower priority wins, a sprite beats a BG of the same priority, and BG0 beats BG3 on ties. The backdrop is a target in both slots.
- **Effects:** alpha blending with EVA/EVB and brightness increase/decrease with EVY. Coefficients 17-31 count as 16. A semi-transparent sprite blends whenever the pixel under it is a second target, whatever the BLDCNT mode. If it doesn't blend, normal BLDCNT handling applies (for example brightness, if OBJ is a first target).
- **BG mosaic:** horizontal mosaic reads the pixel at `x - x % width`. For vertical mosaic, the first line of each block is copied into a new `Ppu` field, `mosaic_source_lines: [[LayerPixel; 240]; 4]` (about 6 KB), and reused for the rest of the block.

The only changes to `mod.rs` are: the old `compose_line` is removed, that field and its initial value are added, and the now-unneeded `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `register()` is dropped.

Dev ROMs, driven with key input through a throwaway runner in the scratchpad:
- **bld-demo:** alpha blending (EVA 8 / EVB 7), brightness increase and brightness decrease all look right on the BG.
- **mos-demo:** BG mosaic looks right for vertical-only and for horizontal plus vertical.
- **win-demo:** the window rectangle shows correctly.
- **prio-demo:** looks plausible; sprites are a stub on this branch.
- **window-midframe:** draws, but there is no reference image to check it against.

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| piugba-gameplay | 0.3233 | **0.9390** (diverging frames 1918 to 1635) |
| tonc-snd1 | 0.9167 | 0.9167 |

No smoke-set test changed. The remaining four games still need grading once memory allows: `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm p3-effects spout-gameplay bulletgba-gameplay celeste-gameplay goodboy-gameplay`. Eight grader containers from other workers were running at the same time, which is the likely cause.

## 3. Unfinished work, guesses and contract changes
- **Mid-frame vertical windows:** gbatek doesn't say what happens when WIN0V/WIN1V change during a frame, so each line is checked on its own against Y1..Y2. window-midframe may want latched behaviour instead.
- **Vertical mosaic shortcut:** the first line of a block is reused exactly as it was drawn, so scroll or affine changes partway through a block are ignored. Doing it exactly would be a contract change: render_line would pass the renderers the block's first line (`line - line % height`) for BGs with mosaic on, and the compositor would only apply horizontal mosaic.
- **OBJ window enable:** I followed gbatek's "Both DISPCNT Bits 12 and 15 must be set", so the OBJ window only counts when OBJ display is on. The comment in render_line says the opposite. If the reference disagrees, it's a one-line change (`obj_window_on`).
- **Effects-disabled windows:** I guessed that turning effects off in a window region also stops semi-transparent sprites from blending there.
- **Contract changes needed:** none that are required. The vertical-mosaic one above is optional.

## 4. Decisions for NOTES.md (2026-11-05)
- The compositor moved into effects.rs as an `impl Ppu` method, to keep the Phase 3 code in one owned file.
- Vertical BG mosaic reuses a stored copy of each block's first line, which avoids changing the renderer contract. Its limit is described in section 3.
- The OBJ window requires both DISPCNT bits 12 and 15, following gbatek.
- Windows are decided per line with no state carried between lines, since gbatek describes no latching.
- A semi-transparent sprite that has no second target below it falls through to normal BLDCNT handling.
